english.notes:
(i)Paragraph 22 of Schedule 4 to the MerchantShipping (Safety of Navigation) Regulations 2002 provides that it shall be a defence for a person charged under theseRegulations to show that he took all reasonable steps to avoid the commissionof the offence.
(ii) Paragraph 21 of Schedule 4to the Merchant Shipping (Safety of Navigation) Regulations 2002 provides thatin relation to paragraph 7 of regulation 10 in Chapter V of the InternationalConvention for the Safety of Life at Sea, it shall bea defence to show that there were compelling reasons not to use a particularmandatory ships' routeing system and that such reasons were recorded in theship's log-book at the time.
(iii) Regulation10(7) of chapter V of the International Convention for the Safety of Life atSea provides that "a ship shall use a mandatory ships' routeing system adoptedby the Organization as required for its category or cargo carried and inaccordance with the relevant provisions in force unless there are compelling reasonsnot to use a particular ships' routeing system. Any such reason shall berecorded in the ships' log".
(iv) Anycontravention of paragraph 7 of regulation 10 in respect of a ship shall be anoffence by the owner, the master of the ship and any other person for the timebeing responsible for the conduct of the ship.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
